Hi Alex —

Great to connect on the product/controls side earlier today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we stay aligned from a security/compliance perspective: 

1) High-level ask from your team
   - Confirm SOC 2 status and timing for Type II (you asked where we are).
   - Clarify GDPR/HIPAA posture for PHI in inference pipelines and data residency options.
   - Evaluate KMS/CMK options (customer-managed keys, HSM support, BYOK flows).

2) What I’m sending over now (attachments + links)

   - vendor-rfi-template.xlsx — if your team prefers, fill this and we’ll respond line-by-line.
   - SOC 2 in-progress letter (high level) — see attached (we’re in final audit prep; Rishi will add detail).

3) Technical clarification we promised on the call (short bullets)
   - In-transit: TLS 1.2+ with modern ciphers, mutual TLS option for dedicated/private deployments.
   - At-rest: AES-256-GCM by default; envelope encryption for model artifacts and customer data.
   - KMS/CMK: support for customer-managed keys via standard cloud KMS integrations (AWS KMS/CMEK, Azure Key Vault, GCP CMEK). We also support HSM-backed flows for PX/PQ integrations depending on deployment.

4) Ask from your side
   - Please share the vendor questionnaire (or confirm you’ll use the attached template).
   - If your crypto team wants a technical deep-dive, suggest a 30–45 min slot next week — Rishi can host.

Next steps I’ll take: attach the RFI and a short SOC note (attached), loop in Marcus for procurement/operator discussions.

Thanks — appreciate the quick sync.

Hi Alex, Neha —

Thanks — a few concrete answers we can provide now; happy to expand on the call.

1) SOC 2
   - Auditor: BluePeak Assurance (audit window Q2–Q3 2027).
   - Type II report: fieldwork scheduled for June; expected availability for customers with NDA in July 2027.

2) Encryption (short technical notes)
   - In-transit: TLS 1.2+ (we recommend TLS 1.3), HSTS enabled. For Dedicated/Private we support mTLS between customer VPC and Redwood nodes.
   - At-rest: primary encryption AES-256-GCM. We use envelope encryption: data encrypted with DEKs (data encryption keys), which are encrypted with CMKs stored in a KMS/HSM.

3) KMS/CMK options — supported modes
   - Customer-managed KMS endpoints (recommended): Redwood can be configured to call your cloud KMS (AWS KMS/GCP KMS/Azure Key Vault) for CMK operations. CMKs remain in your account; Redwood stores only encrypted DEKs.
   - BYOK import into Redwood HSM: For customers requiring Redwood-hosted HSM with imported key material we support HSM-backed CMKs (FIPS 140-2 level 3 hardware options available per contract). This is typically for highly regulated customers; legal + procurement required.
   - Envelope + rotation: DEKs rotated routinely; CMK rotation policy is configurable but we recommend annual rotation for CMKs with automated rewrapping of DEKs.

4) Additional controls
   - Key usage auditing: KMS call logs + our audit trail (token, request id, timestamp) available in the Console and via the Private deployment audit export.
   - Split-key / dual-control: available as an add-on for on-prem deployments and VPC/private setups.

5) Artifacts we’ll share for your intake
   - kms-architecture-diagram.png (attached) — key-flow for BYOK and Redwood-managed flows.
   - a short text file explaining DEK/CMK lifecycle (kms-keyflow.txt).

I can host the 30-minute technical deep dive. Friday 10am PT works for me; Marcus is cc’d for procurement/contract discussion.

—
Rishi Malhotra
